findings.rationale: SC's local outcome prevalence (0.46) is far above what its features imply (mean predicted 0.19): CITL -0.27, a z of -15 on CITL and +10 on prevalence, with AUC normal (0.816), so the labels rather than the model or features are off. The excess is present from round 1 (per-round CITL about -0.66 at round 1 and negative in most rounds). Its update norm grows steadily from about 0.9x to 6x the median, with mostly negative cosine to the median, consistent with a client whose labels disagree with the federation. Subgroup outcomes also show observed/expected about 2 in both sexes, which is the same over-prevalence pattern. The local data is not normal, so this is not classed as poisoning.

KS's observed prevalence (0.374) is roughly double its predicted risk (0.178): CITL -0.197, z -11.2, prevalence z +7.3, ECE z +7.2, with AUC normal (0.805). The CITL is negative in nearly every round, starting at round 1. Its update norm grows from about 0.5x to about 4.5x the median and its cosine to the median is mostly negative. Subgroup outcomes show observed/expected about 2 in both sexes. This is a label/prevalence mismatch rather than a poisoned upload, since its local performance is also off.

VT shows an excess of positives relative to its features: prevalence 0.323 against mean predicted 0.173, CITL -0.150 (z -7.1), with AUC normal (0.834). Two independent tools agree: subgroup outcomes show observed/expected about 2.0 for Sex=0 and 1.85 for Sex=1 (noise-adjusted z 5.8 and 5.3). Its update norms are moderately high (median ratio 1.89, z 3.9) with a negative mean cosine. The evidence is weaker than for SC and KS because VT is smaller (n of about 326 at the final round) and its per-round values are very noisy. Onset is uncertain; round 1 is my best estimate because the CITL is negative in most rounds.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and the three subgroup_outcomes attributes, then confirmed the main suspects with narrower calls. Three clients show a consistent prevalence shift, with observed outcome rates well above what their features imply while AUC stays normal: SC (strongest), KS, and VT (weaker, lower confidence). All three also show anomalous update norms with negative mean cosine to the median. I did not find evidence of poisoning, free-riding, label noise (AUC is normal), subgroup under-diagnosis (observed/expected is above 1, not below), drift, or sentinel-coded missing values. Other flags (for example GU's feature tails, small-subgroup outliers in CT, AK, ME and MI, and single-feature percentile outliers) are small-client noise that did not replicate across tools, so I did not report them. The budget is fully spent (20.0 used).
